walkthroughs.body_html:
Periodic Table & Energy — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Periodic Table & Energy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Periodic Table & Energy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An endothermic reaction can be spontaneous if:
options: ΔS is positive and TΔS > ΔH
ΔS is negative
T is very low
ΔH is very large

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
